We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4{t}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=8t \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =(4{t}^{2})(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)(8t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-4{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8\int t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\operatorname{cos}⁡t & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡t\text{d}t=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,dt \\  & =t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =-4{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8\int t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-4{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t+D) \\  & =-4{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+8\operatorname{cos}⁡t+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=8D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}4{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t & ={[-4{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+8\operatorname{cos}⁡t]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =(0+8(\frac{\pi }{2})(1)+0)-(0+0+8) \\  & =4\pi -8 \\  & =4\pi -8\end{aligned}
$$
